conviction_note: No unpriced, decisive company number was found. The findings net to a small positive (+0.7) because positioning (stock -49% in 20 days, about 17% of float short) and the call's chance to answer the Teradyne question slightly outweigh the second-device slip and margin risks. The scaled number is (2*0.53-1)*19 = +1.14. abs_move is set above the 14.9% event-implied move because the name's confirmed releases moved a median 21.9%. p_up sits only 3 points above 50 because the +11.75 put skew says the opposite and my lean rests on positioning and inference, not a document.
bar: Q1 FY2027 (13 weeks, 2026-06-27 to 2026-09-25) revenue about $27.5m and non-GAAP EPS $0.11. Agreeing sources: Zacks via TradingView $27.5m / $0.11, unchanged over 30 days (https://www.tradingview.com/news/zacks:92d98440e094b:0-aehr-gears-up-to-report-q1-earnings-what-s-in-store-for-the-stock/); MarketBeat $27.53m / $0.11 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-aehr-test-systems-aehr-projected-to-post-quarterly-earnings-on-monday-2026-10-26/); Quiver $27.61m / $0.11. The company gave no Q1 guide, only FY2027 revenue of $130-150m and an 18-22% non-GAAP pre-tax margin (https://www.aehr.com/2026/07/aehr-test-systems-reports-fiscal-2026-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-financial-results/). On the July call the CFO said H1 is likely the same as or better than H2 and Q2 'a very strong quarter'.
positioning_check: Short interest was 5.62M shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, about 2.0 days to cover (https://massive.com/quote/aehr, read 2026-11-02). On 32.66M shares outstanding that is about 17% of float (13.16% at 4.3M on 2026-08-20 per equibles). That counts as crowded, so negatives were shrunk. The skew is +11.75 vol points (25d put IV over 25d call IV), so downside is paid; put/call open interest is 0.5; the event-implied move is 14.89% (straddle 17.08%); 20-day realised vol is 98.5%. The stock is -48.97% over 20 days, -63.4% from its 52-week high of $147.40 and +174.6% above its low. Insiders made only open-market sales: $63.3M over 12 months (CEO $16.0M), no purchases. The October Form 4s checked were RSU tax withholdings (code F), not sales.

findings.finding: The reported quarter should land at or slightly above the $27.5m bar. Q1 FY27 opened with $80.6m of contracted backlog, all of it scheduled to ship within 12 months under the 10-K definition. On 2026-07-14 the CEO said Sonoma package-level shipments start 'during this quarter' with the bulk in Q2. The CFO said H1 is likely the same as or better than H2: on the $130-150m guide that is $65-75m+ for H1, of which consensus puts only $27.5m in Q1. The company has beaten EPS in 3 of the last 4 quarters and matched once; Q4 FY26 printed $18.8m against $17.92m consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 FY26 (2026-07-14) beat revenue, $18.8m vs $17.92m, and set a record for bookings; the stock rose +21.9%, but the move was driven by the first FY27 guide. Q3 FY26 (2026-04-07) +25.7% came with a record $41m order. The 2025-10-06 and 2025-07-08 prints (-17.4%, -12.4%) turned on guidance withdrawal and order timing, not the reported quarter. These are confirmed 8-K 2.02 releases; the fiscal-year change relabels the quarters but does not make them non-events.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus has not moved in 30 days (Zacks ESP 0.00%), so estimates did not react to the CFO's 'first half same or better' remark. The ~$27.5m is roughly 20% of the guide midpoint, which is conservative if H1 is half of the year. If the market expected a large Q1 beat, revisions would have risen and the skew would not be put-heavy. Q1 sits inside the guided year, so a beat mainly confirms the guide; size kept small.
findings.independence: The backlog definition comes from a different document, the FY2026 10-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001040470/000165495426006919/aehr_10k.htm). The cadence comment comes from the call transcript only.

findings.finding: Q1 bookings are at least partly visible: a $22m follow-on wafer-level AI processor order on 2026-08-12, plus a silicon photonics follow-on on 2026-08-04 (amount undisclosed, shipping H1 CY2027). Both fall inside the 06-27 to 09-25 quarter and come on top of the $100.6m effective backlog, which already counted bookings through the first two weeks of FY27. A further ~$6m hyperscaler order arrived on 2026-10-07, after quarter end. Announced orders since the guide therefore lift visibility to roughly $128m+ against a $130-150m year.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Bookings have been the line this stock trades on: the record $60.7m bookings quarter (2026-07-14) rose +21.9%; the $41m order quarter (2026-04-07) rose +25.7%.
findings.why_not_priced: Each order was press-released and is public, so book-to-bill near or above 1 is largely known. What is not public is the unannounced bookings total (Aehr does not release every order) and the ending backlog. Had the market priced strong bookings, the stock would not have fallen 49% in the month the orders accumulated, though that fall is mostly sector-driven (see positioning finding).
findings.independence: Separate PRs: https://www.aehr.com/2026/08/aehr-test-systems-expands-silicon-photonics-production-momentum-with-follow-on-production-order-from-lead-customer/ and https://www.webull.com/news/15706757494473728 (2026-10-07). Shares the backlog base with finding 1.

findings.finding: The lead hyperscaler's second, higher-power AI device has slipped. The April 2026 PR said it was 'expected to move to production later this year'; on the July call it was 'delayed but still expected to start ramping this fiscal year'; the 2026-10-07 PR says 'expected production ramp ... in calendar 2027'. The third device is 'not even this fiscal year'. The slip puts part of the FY27 Sonoma revenue the guide relies on (the CEO put package-level revenue at 'probably $50 million') into H2 FY27 or beyond, which threatens the top of the $130-150m range or a raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2025-07-08 print (-12.4%) and 2025-10-06 print (-17.4%) were guidance-withholding or order-delay prints; per itiger, 'Aehr's Stock Slides After Withholding Guidance, Order Delays'. On this name, delay language on the guide has cost double digits.
findings.why_not_priced: The timing wording moved from 'later this year' (April) to 'calendar 2027' (October) in a press release whose headline was an order. No preview cited the slip; consensus FY numbers are unchanged. Had it been priced, sell-side revisions to FY27 would show, and none appear. Calendar 2027 still sits inside FY27 (ends 2027-06-25), so the guide can hold; that, the crowded short and the ~17% short float shrink the size.
findings.independence: The July call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15228507339449344) independently records the delay. The April PR (https://www.aehr.com/2026/04/aehr-receives-record-41-million-production-order-from-lead-hyperscale-ai-customer-second-half-bookings-exceed-92-million/) gives the original timing.

findings.finding: Part of the October drawdown was attributed to Teradyne's 2026-10-06 launch of Titan HP with burn-in capability; AEHR fell about 11.7% that day to about $92 from $107 on 10-02. Oppenheimer (Outperform, $120) called the overlap limited and the sell-off a buying opportunity. This is the first call since the launch, so management will be asked directly; any customer or order evidence that wafer-level burn-in is untouched would answer a question the price now carries.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on a competitor launch. Oct 27's +11% day on the ~$6m order news shows the stock currently reacts strongly to order evidence.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock is pricing some competitive threat; Titan HP is package-level and system-level test with a burn-in feature, while Aehr's growth engines are wafer-level FOX-XP and package-level Sonoma. If the market saw no threat, AEHR would not have underperformed SOX (-15.7% Oct 6-16) by about 3x. A rebuttal is inference about the call, so the size is small and runs against the +11.75 skew.
findings.independence: Teradyne's own launch coverage (https://finviz.com/news/399372/teradyne-introduces-titan-hp-platform-with-burn-in-capabilities-for-advanced-ai-data-center-devices) and Zacks framing Titan HP's rivals as KLA and Cohu, not Aehr (https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/can-aehr-turn-ai-processor-tests-long-term-revenue-streams).

findings.finding: Into the print the stock is -49% over 20 days and -63% from its high, while short interest rose from 4.3M (13% float, Aug 20) to 5.22M (Sep 30) to 5.62M (Oct 15, about 17% of float, 2.0 days to cover). Most of the drawdown is explained by a sector sell-off: SOX -15.7% from Oct 6 to Oct 16, eight straight down days, AI-buildout doubts and ~5% yields; AEHR has a beta of 3.5. A crowded, growing short into an event the company can use to restate a $130-150m guide gives a squeeze mechanism on any reaffirmation.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last three confirmed prints were +16.0%, +25.7% and +21.9%, and both large up prints came after pullbacks. The 2025-01-13 print (-27.1%) shows the downside tail when guidance disappoints.
findings.why_not_priced: The options market is paying for downside (skew +11.75, 25d puts over calls) despite 17% of float already short. If a reaffirmation squeeze were priced, the skew would be flat or call-side and the short count would be falling. The drawdown has a sector explanation rather than a company one (lesson 5), so this is positioning, not evidence of mispricing; sized small.
findings.independence: Sector cause: https://www.trustnet.com/news/13486948/high-flying-semiconductor-stocks-fall-11-in-a-week-what-investors-need-to-know and https://koalagains.com/daily-top-movers/top-losers/details/fbd65cc5-537e-4ab4-9016-9b5a3fdbe281 (2026-10-16). August short interest from equibles (https://equibles.com/stocks/AEHR).

findings.finding: Insiders sold $63.3M of stock in open-market sales over 12 months with no purchases, $16.0M of it by CEO Gayn Erickson. Most of it was in Aug-Sep 2026 near $127-133, during the quarter being reported. The October Form 4s checked were tax withholdings on RSU vesting (code F, e.g. COO Adil Engineer, 202 shares at $63.95 on 10-27), not sales, and there was no insider buying into the 49% fall.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print can be tied to insider selling.
findings.why_not_priced: The selling is public in Form 4s and widely aggregated, so it is mostly priced. What it adds is that management did not buy at half the price, which is weak evidence that they do not expect a guide raise. Soft inference, sized near zero.
findings.independence: Form 4 code F confirmed at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1040470/000104047026000311/0001040470-26-000311.txt; 12-month totals at https://massive.com/quote/aehr.

findings.finding: Gross margin risk in the quarter: Q4 FY26 non-GAAP gross margin was 45% (FY26 38.5%). Q1-Q2 FY27 is weighted to package-level Sonoma, which the CEO said carries lower margins than wafer-level, and Zacks's preview flags that power supply component prices 'have risen sharply' because suppliers also serve large AI companies. A revenue beat at a lower margin is the 'quality of the beat' trap.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin has not been the line of a past AEHR print in the history; FY26 non-GAAP net income fell to $0.9m from $4.6m on lower revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: The $0.11 EPS consensus on $27.5m revenue implies about a 13% net margin, above the 18-22% pre-tax margin guide only after taxes. Little sell-side discussion of mix or power-supply costs appeared. If priced, EPS estimates would have been cut against an unchanged revenue bar; they are unchanged. This is an inference from the mix, sized small.
findings.independence: Mix comment from the July call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15228507339449344); cost comment from Zacks, which may itself paraphrase the call, so partly one source.

findings.finding: onsemi, historically Aehr's largest silicon carbide customer, reports Q3 2026 the same evening (2026-11-02 amc). Its commentary on SiC automotive and AI data-center demand will be read alongside Aehr's SiC line; Aehr took about $8m of new SiC orders in July.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measured; SiC is now a minority of Aehr's guide, which is AI-led.
findings.why_not_priced: Its outcome is unknown until tonight, and its sign is unknown.

findings.finding: Test-equipment peers that reported after Aehr last spoke showed strong AI-driven test demand. FormFactor (quarter ended 2026-09-26, reported 2026-10-28) beat the high end on revenue ($280.5m), margin and EPS and guided Q4 to $285m +/- $10m. Teradyne's Q3 revenue rose 70% y/y to $1.31bn, above the top of its guide, with Q4 guided 1.8% above consensus. Both stocks still fell after their beats.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None for the peer read-through specifically.
findings.why_not_priced: Peer beats are public; AEHR continued lower (Oct 29 close $61.21, -5.16%) after them, so the read-through is mostly priced. That FORM and TER sold their beats is also a warning about this reaction function. It is a proxy, sized small.

outside_window.finding: The ramp of the lead hyperscaler's second AI device in calendar 2027 and the wafer-level pilot production decision at the 'major AI processor supplier' resolve months after this print. Only commentary on them reaches the window.

baseline_tension: The small net positive runs against the +11.75 put skew. It agrees with the -49% run-up only in the sense that a crowded short into a cut price can squeeze. The positioning lean is not a document, so p_up is held at 53.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (positioning, skew): my net sign is against a +11.75 put skew, so the positioning finding went from +2.0 to +1.2 and p_up from 54 to 53. The crowded short (~17% of float) shrank the second-device-slip negative from -1.5 to -1.2.

Lesson 5 (an unexplained drawdown is worth 0): the drawdown does have a sector explanation (SOX -15.7%), so the positioning finding is kept, but it rests on short interest rather than mispricing, which is another reason it is smaller.
Lesson 6 / core table (inside the guide): the Q1 revenue finding lands inside the FY27 guide, so it went from +1.0 to +0.6. The bar is sourced to three agreeing estimates, so no cap.

Lesson 3 (own caveat): the Teradyne-rebuttal finding admits it is inference about the call, so +0.8 became +0.5. The insider and margin findings went from -0.5 to -0.4 and -1.0 to -0.8 because their own text says they are mostly priced or partly one source.

Lesson 8 and the history note: the baseline reactions are confirmed 8-K 2.02 releases; the fiscal-year change relabels the quarters but does not make them phantom events. abs_move was raised from 18 to 19 against the 21.9% median and the 14.9% implied move.
Lesson 1 (a fact is not a reaction): FORM and TER sold their beats, so the peer read-through stays at +0.4 and print_vs_bar (+4) is allowed to exceed the reaction call.
